Day 1 · Solutions
Solute, solvent and solution
AT S-7-PS-B-02: Relate concentration to the number of solute particles in a given volume of solvent; differentiate dilute and concentrated solutions.
Write on the board
  • Solute: the substance that dissolves (sugar)
  • Solvent: the liquid that does the dissolving (water)
  • Solution: solute + solvent, evenly mixed
  • Dissolve: solute particles spread out between solvent particles
  • The sugar does not vanish. It is still there as tiny particles
Day 1 · Solutions
Concentration: dilute and concentrated
AT S-7-PS-B-02: Relate concentration to the number of solute particles in a given volume of solvent; differentiate dilute and concentrated solutions.
Write on the board
  • Concentration = number of solute particles in a given volume of solvent
  • Same volume, few dots: dilute
  • Same volume, many dots: concentrated
  • Add water: dots stay the same, volume grows, so concentration falls
  • Dilute does not mean weak. Concentrated does not mean thick
Day 2 · Solubility
Solubility, saturated and unsaturated
AT S-7-PS-B-03: Identify the factors that affect solubility and recognise why they matter in homes and industries.
Write on the board
  • Solubility: the maximum mass of solute that dissolves in a given amount of solvent at a given temperature
  • Unsaturated: can still dissolve more solute
  • Saturated: no more solute can dissolve
  • Extra solute stays at the bottom as undissolved crystals
Day 2 · Solubility
Factors that change how much dissolves
AT S-7-PS-B-03: Identify the factors that affect solubility and recognise why they matter in homes and industries.
Write on the board
  • 1. Temperature: most solids dissolve more in hot water
  • 2. Type of solute: sugar, salt and baking soda differ
  • 3. Type of solvent: sugar and salt dissolve in water, not in oil
  • Gases are the opposite: less dissolves when hot (fizzy drinks go flat)
  • Homes: chai, washing powder. Industry: dyeing, sugar mills, syrups

Day 2 · Temperature and particles
Temperature and particle motion
Higher temperature means more kinetic energy, faster particles and more collisions.
Day 1 and 2 · Terminology
Terms that are easily mixed up
Pair
First term
Second term
Dilute vs concentrated
Dilute: few solute particles in the volume
Concentrated: many solute particles in the volume
Concentrated vs saturated
Concentrated: lots of solute per volume, may still take more
Saturated: no more can dissolve at that temperature
Unsaturated vs saturated
Unsaturated: can still dissolve more
Saturated: full, extra stays as crystals
Solubility vs concentration
Solubility: the limit (maximum that can dissolve)
Concentration: the amount actually dissolved now
Day 3 · Rate of dissolving
Three ways to speed up dissolving
AT S-7-PS-B-04: Identify ways of speeding up dissolving in a given amount of water and give reasons.
Write on the board
  • Rate = how fast it dissolves
  • Solubility = how much dissolves
  • Heating, stirring and crushing speed it up
  • Stirring and crushing do not change how much can dissolve in the end
  • Fair test: change one thing, keep the rest the same
Method
Particle reason
Effect
Heating
Particles move faster, more collisions
Faster; also more can dissolve
Stirring
Brings fresh solvent to the surface
Faster only
Crushing
More surface area exposed
Faster only
Day 3 · Rate of dissolving
Smaller pieces, larger surface area
AT S-7-PS-B-04: Identify ways of speeding up dissolving in a given amount of water and give reasons.
Write on the board
  • Cut a cube into 8 smaller cubes: surface area doubles (24 to 48 cm²)
  • More surface touching water means more collisions
  • So smaller pieces dissolve faster
  • Crushing does not add more sugar. It only saves time
